newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian transport unions call off strike action.
newsitem.headline: Italian transport unions call off strike action.

text.p: Italian transport unions called off a planned nationwide strike on Thursday after all-night talks, and said further negotiations would be held with employers next week to try to find a lasting solution.
Transport union leaders said they had reached an agreement with local public transport companies which will pave the way to end lengthy and bitter contract disputes.
Some 120,000 local public bus, tram and metro drivers had called the strike for Thursday to put pressure on companies and government to renew contracts which expired over 15 months ago.
Italy is currently plagued by a string of strikes. Air traffic controllers stopped work this week and plan further action in Milan on April 18.
A wildcat bus drivers' strike in Rome on Tuesday brought the city to a standstill as commuters struggled to reach work.

A four-day sea transport strike was due to start on April 19. Railway workers have called a 24-hour stoppage on the same day. A four-day strike by petrol pump attendants, unhappy with moves to reorganise the sector, is planned for next Monday.
